study_archetype: single-patient in vivo imaging-based computational FSI modeling study

reported_items.raw_name: Objective: assess effects of anisotropic vessel properties and cyclic bending on plaque mechanics
Study design: in vivo IVUS imaging combined with computational modeling (FSI) on one patient dataset
Data/sample: 44-slice in vivo IVUS dataset from one coronary plaque (one patient)
Methods: construction of four 3-D fluid–structure interaction (FSI) models varying anisotropy, cyclic bending, and axial stretch
Outcomes: reported maximum principal stress (P1) comparisons and flow behavior changes (percent differences)
Results: quantitative comparisons — model 2: +63% P1, model 3: +126% P1, model 4: +345% P1 vs model 1; cyclic bending effects on flow 5%–15%
reported_items.sub_category: relative changes in stress and flow
